title: The Adventure of the Bruce-Partington Plans
description: A dense yellow fog has settled over London, and the theft of top-secret submarine plans from Woolwich Arsenal has led to the mysterious death of a young clerk, Niffler Them Dungbomb. Detective Malfoy Harry must unravel the conspiracy before the plans fall into foreign hands.
intro_narrative: In the third week of November, 1895, a thick fog blankets London. Malfoy Harry, restless and bored, is drawn into a case of national importance when his brother Albus arrives with news of the theft of the Bruce-Partington submarine plans and the death of a young clerk, Niffler Them Dungbomb. The plans, some of which are still missing, were found on Dungbomb's body near Aldgate Station. Harry must navigate a web of treachery, foreign agents, and government secrets to uncover the truth.

required_evidence: Bruce-Partington submarine plans (all three missing plans)
Daily Telegraph newspaper clippings (advertisements linking Dursley and Sorting)
required_motive: Financial gain (Colonel Sorting's Stock Exchange debt)
Espionage (Where Dursley's sale of plans to foreign agents)

phases.name: Initial Investigation
phases.objective: Gather initial clues and speak to key witnesses in Baker Street and Aldgate Station.

phases.name: Woolwich Arsenal Inquiry
phases.objective: Investigate the office where the plans were stolen and interview suspects at Woolwich Arsenal.

phases.name: Kensington and Gloucester Road
phases.objective: Explore Dursley's residence and the Underground connections to uncover the method of the crime.

phases.name: Final Confrontation
phases.objective: Set a trap at Charing Cross Hotel to capture the culprits and recover the missing plans.

malfoy_harry.persona: Sharp, observant, and deductive. Speaks in a precise, almost arrogant manner, with a dry wit. Impatient with those slower to understand his reasoning.
malfoy_harry.abilities: Master of deduction, disguise, and forensic analysis. Skilled in lock-picking and observation.

knowledge_about_others.albus_harry: Knows Albus is the most indispensable man in the British government, though he pretends to be a subordinate.
knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: Suspects his involvement due to his access to the keys and financial troubles.
knowledge_about_others.where_dursley: Believes Dursley is the foreign agent responsible for the theft and murder.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Realizes the body was placed on the train roof from Dursley's window. Plans to set a trap at Charing Cross Hotel.

tonks.persona: Loyal, curious, and pragmatic. Often serves as the voice of reason and provides a grounding perspective for Harry's theories.
tonks.abilities: Skilled in note-taking, research, and discreet observation. Acts as Harry's moral compass.

knowledge_about_others.miss_diggory_karkaroff: Sympathizes with her grief and believes in Dungbomb's innocence.

albus_harry.persona: Solemn, authoritative, and highly intelligent. Speaks in a measured, deliberate manner, often with a hint of dry humor. Rarely leaves his routine.
albus_harry.secret: He is the central figure in British intelligence, often referred to as 'the British government.' His involvement in the case is due to the national importance of the stolen plans.

knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: Knows of his financial troubles and access to the keys but does not suspect him initially.
knowledge_about_others.where_dursley: Aware of Dursley's reputation as a foreign agent but lacks concrete evidence.

niffler_them_dungbomb.persona: Hot-headed but patriotic. Described as single-minded and chivalrous by his fiancée.
niffler_them_dungbomb.secret: His sudden disappearance and death are central to the mystery. His actions on the night of his death are suspicious, but his true motives remain unclear.

knowledge_about_others.fenrir_rubeus: Worked closely with Rubeus and may have suspected his involvement in the theft.
knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: May have seen Sorting with the stolen plans.

colonel_snitch_sorting.persona: Charming and well-spoken, but desperate due to financial troubles. Acts with a sense of entitlement and arrogance.
colonel_snitch_sorting.secret: He stole the plans to pay off a Stock Exchange debt and conspired with Where Dursley. He is responsible for Dungbomb's death, though he claims it was an accident.

knowledge_about_others.where_dursley: Worked with Dursley to sell the plans to foreign agents.
knowledge_about_others.sir_fleur_sorting: Used his brother's keys to access the plans.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Confesses to his role in the theft and murder when confronted with the evidence. Reveals Dursley's location.

where_dursley.persona: Smooth, calculating, and ruthless. Speaks with a foreign accent and carries himself with an air of superiority.
where_dursley.secret: He orchestrated the theft of the Bruce-Partington plans and murdered Dungbomb to cover his tracks. He is attempting to sell the plans to foreign governments.

knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: Conspired with Sorting to steal the plans.
knowledge_about_others.niffler_them_dungbomb: Killed Dungbomb to prevent him from exposing the theft.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Attempts to flee when confronted but is captured at Charing Cross Hotel.

sir_fleur_sorting.persona: Stoic, patriotic, and highly respected. His death is shrouded in mystery and linked to the theft of the plans.
sir_fleur_sorting.secret: His keys were used to steal the plans, but it is unclear whether he was complicit or a victim.

knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: His brother, who may have used his keys to access the plans.

fenrir_rubeus.persona: Silent, morose, and unpopular with colleagues. Speaks in a gruff, dismissive manner.
fenrir_rubeus.secret: He was the last person to lock up the office on the night of the theft. His whereabouts and actions are suspicious.

knowledge_about_others.niffler_them_dungbomb: Worked closely with Dungbomb and may have had a motive to frame him.
knowledge_about_others.colonel_snitch_sorting: May have seen Sorting near the office on the night of the theft.

miss_diggory_karkaroff.persona: Grieving but determined to clear her fiancé's name. Speaks with emotion and sincerity.
miss_diggory_karkaroff.secret: She knows more about Dungbomb's state of mind on the night of his death than she initially reveals.

knowledge_about_others.niffler_them_dungbomb: Noticed his nervous behavior and hints about the importance of the plans.

thestral.persona: Professional, methodical, and slightly impatient with Harry's unorthodox methods. Speaks in a no-nonsense manner.
thestral.abilities: Skilled in forensic analysis and legal procedures. Provides official support to Harry's investigation.

knowledge_about_others.where_dursley: Suspects Dursley's involvement but lacks evidence.

baker_street.description: A cozy, cluttered sitting-room at 221B Baker Street, filled with books, chemical apparatus, and the lingering scent of pipe tobacco. The dense fog outside obscures the view from the windows.
baker_street.setting: A dimly lit, Victorian-era sitting-room with a fireplace crackling softly. The walls are lined with bookshelves, and a large armchair sits near the window. A desk is piled high with papers and notes.
clues: Advertisements in the *Daily Telegraph* agony column linking Dursley and Sorting.

people.name: Malfoy Harry
people.description: A tall, lean man with sharp features and piercing eyes. He paces restlessly, his mind clearly occupied with the case.
people.notes: The detective in charge of the investigation. His deductive skills are unmatched, but he is impatient with those who cannot keep up with his reasoning.

people.name: Tonks
people.description: A sturdy, reliable figure with a keen eye for detail. He sits near the desk, taking notes.
people.notes: Harry's loyal assistant and chronicler. He provides a grounding perspective and often serves as Harry's moral compass.

people.name: Albus Harry
people.description: A tall, portly man with a masterful brow and alert, steel-grey eyes. He exudes an air of authority and intelligence.
people.notes: Harry's brother and a high-ranking government official. His involvement signals the national importance of the case.

people.name: Thestral
people.description: A thin, austere man with a professional demeanor. He carries himself with the confidence of a Scotland Yard detective.
people.notes: A detective from Scotland Yard who assists Harry in the investigation. He is methodical and slightly skeptical of Harry's unorthodox methods.

objects.name: Desk
objects.description: A large, cluttered desk covered in papers, notes, and chemical apparatus. A pipe and tobacco pouch sit near the edge.
objects.notes: Harry's primary workspace. Contains notes and clues related to the case.

objects.name: Bookshelf
objects.description: A tall bookshelf filled with volumes on crime, chemistry, and history. Some books are stacked haphazardly on top of others.
objects.notes: Contains Harry's extensive collection of reference materials.

objects.name: Armchair
objects.description: A well-worn armchair near the fireplace, its cushions slightly flattened from frequent use.
objects.notes: Harry's favorite spot for thinking and relaxing.

objects.name: Emerald Tie-Pin
objects.description: A small, intricately designed emerald tie-pin. It gleams faintly in the firelight.
objects.notes: A reward given to Harry for solving the case. It is said to be a gift from a gracious lady.

objects.name: Dark Lantern
objects.description: A small, portable lantern with a shutter to control the light. It is designed for discreet use.
objects.notes: A tool used by Harry for nighttime investigations.

objects.name: Revolver
objects.description: A sleek, well-maintained revolver. It is loaded and ready for use.
objects.notes: Harry's weapon of choice for dangerous situations.

aldgate_station.description: A dimly lit Underground station, shrouded in fog. The tracks stretch into the darkness, and the platform is eerily quiet. A body was found here, near the edge of the tracks.
aldgate_station.setting: A narrow, grimy platform with tiled walls. The tracks curve out of a tunnel, and the air is thick with the scent of coal and damp. A single gas lamp flickers weakly.
clues: Body found near Aldgate Station with no ticket in pocket.
The absence of bleeding on the railway line where the body was found.

objects.name: Platform Bench
objects.description: A wooden bench on the platform, its paint chipped and worn. It offers a place to sit and observe the tracks.
objects.notes: A potential spot for witnesses to have seen something unusual.

objects.name: Ticket Booth
objects.description: A small, enclosed booth where tickets are sold. The window is slightly ajar, and papers are scattered inside.
objects.notes: The clerk may have seen Dungbomb purchase a ticket.

contains.name: Dungbomb's Ticket Stub
contains.description: A torn ticket stub with the time and destination partially legible.
contains.notes: Evidence that Dungbomb purchased a ticket to London Bridge.

objects.name: Railway Tracks
objects.description: The tracks curve out of the tunnel and stretch into the distance. The rails gleam faintly in the dim light.
objects.notes: The body was found near this spot, with no signs of bleeding on the line.

woolwich_arsenal.description: A secure government office building where the Bruce-Partington plans were kept. The atmosphere is tense, with officials whispering in the hallways.
woolwich_arsenal.setting: A large, austere building with long corridors and locked offices. The air smells of ink and paper, and the walls are lined with filing cabinets.
clues: Seven of the ten stolen Bruce-Partington plans found on Dungbomb's body.
Three missing, essential plans not found on Dungbomb.
Dungbomb's sudden disappearance into the fog near the office.
Dungbomb's nervous and excited behavior when purchasing a train ticket.

people.name: Fenrir Rubeus
people.description: A thin, gruff man with bespectacled eyes and haggard cheeks. He twitches nervously as he speaks.
people.notes: The senior clerk at Woolwich Arsenal. He was the last to lock up the office on the night of the theft.

people.name: Niffler Them Dungbomb
people.description: A young man with a determined expression. His body lies in the morgue, but his presence lingers in the office.
people.notes: The victim of the case. His actions on the night of his death are suspicious.

people.name: Miss Diggory Karkaroff
people.description: A white-faced young lady with tear-stained cheeks. She clutches a handkerchief tightly.
people.notes: Dungbomb's fiancée. She is determined to clear his name.

objects.name: Safe
objects.description: A large, burglar-proof safe with an intricate lock. The door is slightly ajar, and the interior is empty.
objects.notes: Contained the Bruce-Partington plans before they were stolen.

contains.name: False Keys
contains.description: A set of keys that appear to be duplicates of the safe and office keys.
contains.notes: Used to access the safe and office on the night of the theft.

objects.name: Dungbomb's Desk
objects.description: A cluttered desk with papers, a check-book, and theatre tickets. A small tin cash-box sits near the edge.
objects.notes: Contains personal items belonging to Dungbomb.

contains.name: Dungbomb's Check-Book
contains.description: A check-book from the Woolwich branch of the Capital and Counties Bank. It establishes Dungbomb's identity.
contains.notes: Used to confirm Dungbomb's identity after his death.

contains.name: Dungbomb's Theatre Tickets
contains.description: Two dress-circle tickets for the Woolwich Theatre, dated for the night of Dungbomb's disappearance.
contains.notes: Provided an alibi attempt for Dungbomb's whereabouts.

contains.name: Tin Cash-Box
contains.description: A small tin box containing calculations related to the submarine plans.
contains.notes: Contains technical notes that may link to the stolen plans.

objects.name: Office Window
objects.description: A large window with iron shutters. The shutters are slightly ajar, and the sill is covered in soot.
objects.notes: The window overlooks the railway tracks and may have been used to place the body on the train.

caulfield_gardens.description: A row of grand, middle-Victorian houses in Kensington. Number 13 is dark and seemingly unoccupied, but signs of recent activity are evident.
caulfield_gardens.setting: A line of flat-faced, pillared houses with porticoed entrances. The fog obscures the upper floors, and the street is eerily quiet.
clues: Blood marks found on the window sill and stair of Dursley's residence.
Soot marks on the window sill of Dursley's residence indicating body placement.
Train frequently stops beneath Dursley's back window, allowing placement of the body on the roof.

people.name: Where Dursley
people.description: A smooth, well-dressed man with a foreign accent. He carries himself with an air of superiority.
people.notes: A foreign agent responsible for the theft of the plans and the murder of Dungbomb.

people.name: Colonel Snitch Sorting
people.description: A tall, handsome man with a light beard. His eyes are wild, and his cheeks are stained with tears.
people.notes: The brother of the deceased Sir Fleur Sorting. He is desperate due to financial troubles and involved in the theft.

objects.description: A narrow window sill coated in soot from passing trains. Blood marks and scratches are visible.
objects.notes: Evidence that the body was placed on the train roof from this window.

objects.name: Study Desk
objects.description: A large desk littered with papers, books, and a small tin cash-box. The drawers are slightly ajar.
objects.notes: Contains correspondence and notes related to the theft.

contains.name: *Daily Telegraph* Clippings
contains.description: Newspaper clippings from the agony column, containing coded messages between Dursley and Sorting.
contains.notes: Links Dursley and Sorting in the conspiracy.

objects.name: Life-Preserver
objects.description: A short, weighted club used as a weapon. It is stained with blood.
objects.notes: The murder weapon used by Dursley to kill Dungbomb.

charing_cross_hotel.setting: A lavish hotel with ornate decorations and plush furnishings. The smoking-room is dimly lit, with leather armchairs and a faint scent of tobacco.
